Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred while the pateint was
changing lanes. Complaints centered on neck and low back pain with associated muscle
spasm and reduced range of motion. Mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported
crash, and the presenting symptoms are a plausible result of that force. Physical
examination and imaging findings clearly confirm soft tissue injury to the cervical
and lumbar regions. No prior injury to these body areas is known from the patient's
history or available records.
Care consisted of 20 visits including manual therapy, a home stretching and
strengthening program, and anti-inflammatory medicatoin as needed. Treatment followed
a usual and expected course, with frequency tapering as the patient's pain and
mobility improved. Billing records reflect single entries for each service with no
repeated charges for the same procedure on the same date.
At the most recent visit the patient reported substantial improvement, with
near-normal range of motion and minimal residual discomfort. Dischrage from active
care is recommended, with a home exercise program to be continued independently.
